clue.text: Moderately rich oil producer on holiday

parts.note: an oil well is what brings up crude oil
someone off work is away on holiday

explanation.surface: A modestly wealthy oil tycoon is away on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being comfortably well-to-do means having a fair but not vast amount of money.

clue.text: He may give a seat to someone standing

definitions.text: He may give a seat to someone standing

parts.words: He may give a seat to someone standing
parts.note: sounds like a polite passenger, but describes a voter giving a parliamentary seat to a candidate

explanation.surface: A courteous man offers his seat to a passenger left on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing' means standing for election, and 'seat' is a seat in parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter helps put a candidate into a parliamentary seat by casting a ballot.

clue.text: A staggering situation for those who are left in it

definitions.text: A staggering situation for those who are left in it

parts.words: A staggering situation for those who are left in it
parts.note: a stagger is a sudden ..., and those deserted are left in the ...

explanation.surface: A shocking predicament for anyone who is abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sudden stagger, and appears in the idiom for being abandoned in trouble.

clue.text: Fear led to new form of government

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of fear led are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Fear prompted a new constitution.
explanation.definitionFit: A system uniting self-governing states under a central authority is this kind of rule.

clue.text: Two animals seen here in their element

parts.note: the first beast is a wolf
the second beast is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Two creatures are spotted in their natural habitat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Their element' suggests a natural habitat, but element here is a chemical one: wolfram is another name for tungsten.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is the older name for tungsten, a chemical element with symbol W.

clue.text: Whole rounds or portions

parts.note: bits are pieces or portions

explanation.surface: Complete servings or just parts of them.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is a complete circuit around a body, a whole round.

clue.text: Such farm products are supplied without batteries

definitions.text: Such farm products are supplied without batteries

parts.words: Such farm products are supplied without batteries
parts.note: sounds like toys sold without batteries, but battery cages are what such hens avoid

explanation.surface: Agricultural gadgets sold with no batteries included.
explanation.walkthrough: A battery is also a set of cages for intensively farmed hens.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs or chickens from birds allowed to roam outdoors rather than caged are described this way.

clue.text: Performer's attire's fantastic

definitions.note: performer's is read as performer is, so the definition is the noun performer

indicators.note: fantastic suggests the letters of attire's run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: The entertainer's costume is amazing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a polished term for a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Virus leads to a developing lameness, producing complaint

parts.note: a germ is a microbe such as a virus

indicators.note: developing shows the letters of a lameness changing into a new form

explanation.surface: A virus brings on a growing limp, causing illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella is an infectious illness, and complaint is a term for an ailment.

clue.text: Harbour transport

definitions.meaning: to harbour a grudge is to carry or hold it within oneself
to transport something is to carry it

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to carry: holding a feeling inside, or physically conveying a load.

clue.text: Large air intake

parts.note: read plainly as a description of a big gulp of air taken into the lungs

explanation.definitionFit: Filling the lungs fully before an effort is taking a big inhalation.

clue.text: He attacks the copper with acid

definitions.text: He attacks the copper with acid

parts.words: He attacks the copper with acid
parts.note: sounds like an assault on a policeman, but describes an engraver biting a copper plate with acid

explanation.surface: A thug throws acid at a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman; here it is the metal plate an engraver eats into with acid to make a print.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraver who uses acid on a metal plate to make printing designs is a printmaker of this kind.

clue.text: Smartest form of bedding

indicators.note: a new form of the word smartest means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The most stylish kind of bed linen.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded base for sleeping on is part of the bedding on a bed.

clue.text: Coming to grips with the opposition

definitions.text: Coming to grips with the opposition

parts.words: Coming to grips with the opposition
parts.note: sounds like tackling a problem, but literally means grappling with an opponent

explanation.surface: Finally getting to understand one's rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport of grappling consists of two opponents literally gripping one another.

clue.text: She cleans out for the steward

indicators.note: out signals the letters of she cleans are put out of order

explanation.surface: A cleaning woman tidies up on behalf of the household manager.
explanation.definitionFit: In a medieval great house the official managing the household was a senior steward.

clue.text: Line of peaks and points

parts.note: E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: A ridge of summits and sharp tips.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American mountain range is a long chain of peaks.

clue.text: Union notices exclude Poles

parts.note: to ban is to exclude or prohibit
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Trade union posters bar Polish workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union; it is marriage. Banns are the announcements of an intended wedding read in a British parish church.
explanation.definitionFit: Banns are public announcements in church of a coming marriage, inviting objections.

clue.text: Article on a crime wave discovered in the Western hemisphere

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: wave tells us the letters of a crime ripple into a new order

explanation.surface: A news article on a spate of offences found in the West.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent found by Europeans in 1492 lies in the Western hemisphere.

clue.text: Call to mind

parts.note: sounds like remembering, but read as a call telling someone to mind, take care

explanation.definitionFit: Shouting 'mind!' is a warning to take care and watch out.

clue.text: Separated and sure to play around

indicators.note: letters that play around move about, so and sure are rearranged

explanation.surface: Split up, and certain to sleep with other people.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means apart or into pieces, as in torn apart.

clue.text: Moral support

definitions.meaning: a vertical post holding something up

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both honest and principled, and a vertical prop or post.

clue.text: Get ready for the spring

parts.note: sounds like preparing for the season, but means preparing to leap

explanation.surface: Prepare for the coming season.
explanation.definitionFit: Bending low with legs tensed is how an animal prepares to leap.

clue.text: Hands and feet, for example

parts.note: sounds like body parts, but hands (used for horses) and feet are units of length

explanation.surface: Body extremities given as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand (four inches) and a foot (twelve inches) are both units of length.

clue.text: The Lord's judge

parts.note: sounds like God as judge, but Lord's is the London cricket ground, where an official adjudicates

explanation.surface: God as the judge of all.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's famous cricket ground; the judge there is the match official who gives batsmen out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket match official rules on dismissals, so acts as the judge on the field.

clue.text: It may hold up current supplies

definitions.text: It may hold up current supplies

parts.words: It may hold up current supplies
parts.note: sounds like something delaying stock, but current is electricity carried on cables held aloft

explanation.surface: Something that might delay existing stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall steel tower carries overhead cables delivering electricity.

clue.text: Forever aimless

definitions.meaning: end in the sense of purpose or aim, so lacking a goal

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means unending, and also, taking end as purpose, lacking an aim.

clue.text: Insulates, say, the boiler but is in no hurry

definitions.meaning: wrapping a boiler or pipes in insulating material

explanation.surface: A plumber wraps the boiler but takes his time about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap pipes in insulation and to trail behind slowly share one spelling.

clue.text: Agree to start home without me calling in pursuit

parts.note: two accounts that tally agree

indicators.note: home without me says the letters of me are taken away

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Agreeing to set off home without the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry is the huntsman's shout when the fox is sighted during a chase.

clue.text: Essay I can turn in at Oxford or Cambridge

indicators.note: the pieces go in the middle of the word for essay

parts.note: to essay something is to try it

indicators.note: turning the word for can makes it read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A student's essay attempt turned in at a top university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' links to the definition: both Oxford and Cambridge have a college of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinity College exists at both ancient universities, so the name fits either.
